title: Evolution, structural diversity and functional plasticity of plant derived multifunctional proteases and alpha-amylases inhibitors.
authors: Dongare, Pratiksha M; Madage, Varsha A; Deshpande, Neha V; Giri, Ashok P; Pawar, Pankaj K
one_liner_zh: 综述植物来源多功能蛋白酶和α-淀粉酶抑制剂的结构多样性、进化及功能可塑性，并提及分子对接、MD和AlphaFold等计算结构生物学方法的应用，但核心对象非蛋白质结构计算建模本身，而是抑制剂功能综述。
abstract: Plant derived multifunctional inhibitors (MFIs) are an important class of plant defense proteins that disrupt insect digestion by simultaneously impairing protein and carbohydrate catabolism. With the increasing knowledge of inhibitors of plant enzymes, MFIs have become a separate functional group. In this review we propose an extended definition that encompasses the classical inhibitors acting on structurally unrelated enzymes and also inhibitors acting on enzymes of the same substrate pathway, e.g. alpha-amylase/alpha-glucosidase and trypsin/chymotrypsin systems. Most of the MFIs consist of single polypeptide chains with spatially separated inhibitory sites, which allow simultaneous inhibition of several enzyme targets. The structural organization, inhibitory mechanism and evolutionary diversification of these inhibitors are reviewed with emphasis on the major families including Bowman-Birk, Kunitz-type and cereal trypsin/alpha-amylase inhibitors. Their domain architecture, disulfide bond patterns and structure-function relationships are discussed in view of their remarkable stability and functional versatility. Recent advances in computational structural biology, including molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and AlphaFold-based protein structure prediction, have promoted mechanistic insights and enabled structure-guided engineering of improved inhibitors. The review also discusses the evolutionary origin of MFIs through gene duplication, domain shuffling, sequence diversification and adaptive evolution, and emerging approaches such as protein engineering, recombinant expression, synthetic biology and genome editing. Finally, the applications in crop protection, development of biopesticides and food biotechnology, as well as the challenges regarding insect adaptation, evolution of resistance, biosafety and ecological impacts are critically discussed. Bridging current gaps in structural characterization and in vivo validation is necessary for the translation of MFIs into sustainable agricultural and biotechnological applications.
abstract_zh: 植物来源的多功能抑制剂（MFIs）是一类重要的植物防御蛋白，通过同时损害蛋白质和碳水化合物分解代谢来干扰昆虫消化。随着对植物酶抑制剂认识的不断深入，MFIs已成为一个独立的功能群。在本综述中，我们提出一个扩展定义，涵盖作用于结构无关酶的经典抑制剂，以及作用于同一底物途径酶的抑制剂，例如α-淀粉酶/α-葡萄糖苷酶和胰蛋白酶/胰凝乳蛋白酶系统。大多数MFIs由具有空间分离抑制位点的单条多肽链组成，这使得它们能够同时抑制多个酶靶标。本文综述了这些抑制剂的结构组织、抑制机制和进化多样化，重点介绍了主要家族，包括Bowman-Birk、Kunitz型和谷物胰蛋白酶/α-淀粉酶抑制剂。鉴于其显著的稳定性和功能多样性，我们讨论了它们的结构域架构、二硫键模式及结构-功能关系。计算结构生物学的最新进展，包括分子对接、分子动力学模拟和基于AlphaFold的蛋白质结构预测，促进了机制洞察，并实现了对改进抑制剂的结构引导工程改造。本综述还讨论了MFIs通过基因复制、结构域重排、序列多样化和适应性进化产生的进化起源，以及新兴方法，如蛋白质工程、重组表达、合成生物学和基因组编辑。最后，批判性讨论了在作物保护、生物农药开发和食品生物技术中的应用，以及昆虫适应、抗性进化、生物安全和生态影响方面的挑战。弥合结构表征和体内验证方面的现有差距，对于将MFIs转化为可持续农业和生物技术应用是必要的。
